examples.text: Au jour naissant, il [le fleuve] apparaît comme un miroir d’argent que le souffle a terni ; les feux de midi le font rayonner et, quand le soleil décline, il se revêt de nacre ainsi que les coquilles où chante encore la mer.
Le soleil commençait à rayonner sur la cime des montagnes.

Vient mai ! On est heureux alors de respirer les bouffées d’air frais qui montent dans la nuit, de sentir sur son dos la réverbération des murs brûlés de soleil et qui, le soir venu, laissent rayonner leur tiédeur.

Pons réchauffé reprit forme humaine : la couleur vitale revint aux yeux, la chaleur extérieure rappela le mouvement dans les organes, Schmucke fit boire à Pons de l’eau de mélisse mêlée à du vin, l’esprit de la vie s’infusa dans ce corps, l’intelligence rayonna de nouveau sur ce front naguère insensible comme une pierre.
Sous l’action d’une pensée indevinable, elle a rougi. J’ai vu l’onde sanguine se propager à son visage ; j’ai vu rayonner son cœur.

glosses: Faire sentir son action sur une certaine étendue.

examples.text: De ce point central, l’armée rayonnait sur les pays voisins.

Le salon, ce noyau de conservateurs appartenant à tous les partis, et qui grossissait journellement, eut bientôt une grande influence. Par la diversité de ses membres, et surtout grâce à l’impulsion secrète que chacun d’eux recevait du clergé, il devint le centre réactionnaire qui rayonna sur Plassans entier.
Là, le mythe aurait acquis sa force de crédibilité, qui lui aurait permis de rayonner sur les jeunes salariées.
J’ai fait rayonner cette pièce pour y mettre mes livres.
J'ai fini de rayonner la roue pour le vélo de ma femme qui démarre le vélotaf à la rentrée.
On l'utilise ainsi pour rayonner la roue, retendre les rayons pour la dévoiler , résorber un saut, etc.
Moi aussi, j'ai bricolé grave pour rayonner la roue avant de mon poney.

glosses: elektromagnetische oder radioaktive Strahlung emittieren oder reflektieren

examples.text: Der Atommüll, den wir heute produzieren, wird noch hunderttausende von Jahren strahlen.
[Fukushima:] „Straßen und Orte wurden gereinigt und freigegeben, obwohl die Erde immer noch strahlte.“

Röntgen war verblüfft: Das Glas war weiter entfernt, als die Kathodenstrahlung eigentlich reichen sollte, und selbst wenn er zwischen die Kathode und das Glas ein Kohlepapier oder ein Holzbrettchen hielt, strahlte das Glas doch weiter.
So wie du strahlst gibt es wohl gute Neuigkeiten?
Dem Prinzen gelang es nicht auf Anhieb, seiner Gemahlin den Trauring auf den Finger zu stecken. Trotz der kleinen Panne strahlte die Prinzessin über das ganze Gesicht.

glosses: in alle Richtungen, meist durch die Luft und meist über Wellen, verbreiten und aussenden

examples.text: Tschernobyl strahlt noch bis heute Radioaktivität aus.

glosses: einen ganz bestimmten Eindruck machen (der durch das Objekt näher beschrieben wird)

examples.text: Er strahlt Ruhe aus.
In diesem Moment strahlte sie nichts anders als reine Panik aus.
„Als habe jemand einen Schalter umgelegt, war es wieder da, das Charisma, das er schon in Chicago ausgestrahlt hatte.“

glosses: Nachrichten oder auch Informationen senden und damit der Allgemeinheit zugänglich machen

examples.text: Die Nachrichten wurden pünktlich ausgestrahlt.

glosses: To extend, send or spread out from a center like radii.

examples.text: Crewe North Motive Power Depot is to be modernised completely. This includes the provision of a new coaling plant, ash handling plant, and two new locomotive sheds of the latest roundhouse type, each with 32 roads radiating from a 70-ft. dia. turntable.
Oban is not a terminus; its routes radiate by sea, rail and road.
Doncaster is a rail hub in every sense. Passenger lines radiate in six directions, there are freight lines that bypass the station, extensive freight yards, a major works, and a rolling stock depot.
The stove radiates heat.

glosses: To come out or proceed in rays or waves.

examples.text: The heat radiates from a stove.
Light radiates from luminous bodies directly to our eyes.
She raised her head, and carefully opened her eyes again, staring directly into the orange glow radiating through the thick glass.

glosses: To expose to ionizing radiation, such as by radiography.
To manifest oneself in a glowing manner.

examples.text: Slim, sensual Richard Hell radiates a commanding coolness.

glosses: To spread into new habitats, migrate.

examples.text: Programmes marked thus will be radiated by Droitwich, but not by London and North National transmitters.

glosses: Radiating from a center; having rays or parts diverging from a center; radiated.

examples.text: a radiate crystal

glosses: Surrounded by rays, such as the head of a saint in a religious picture; (heraldry) radiant.

examples.text: […] and (2) the radiate or Eastern crown, usually five rays being shown. The see of Ely bears the apocryphal coat of St. Ethelreda: gules, three open crowns or. Azure, three open crowns or, are the arms of[…]
On a wreath of the colors argent and tenné four lightning flashes barbed radiate pilewise of the first, a Roman helm or garnished gules.

glosses: Having parts radiating from the center, like the petals in many flowers.
Consisting of a disc in which the florets are tubular.
Having radial symmetry, like a sea star.
The technology that allows for the transmission of sound or other signals by modulation of electromagnetic waves.

examples.text: send a message by radio

glosses: A device that can capture (receive) the signal sent over radio waves and render the modulated signal as sound.

examples.text: We heard a lovely song on the radio.
She was listening to the radio when he knocked on the door.

glosses: Any audio playing device, such as the on-board entertainment system in a car, usually including a radio receiver as well as the capability to play audio from recorded media; see also car radio.

examples.text: David Bowie's classic hit Space Oddity will be looping on the radio as the car is hurled into an elliptical orbit that stretches out to Mars' orbit around the Sun.

glosses: A device that can transmit radio signals.
The continuous broadcasting of sound via the Internet in the style of traditional radio.
To use two-way radio to transmit (a message) (to another radio or other radio operator).

examples.text: I think the boat is sinking; we'd better radio for help. / I radioed him already. / Radio the coordinates this time. / OK. I radioed them the coordinates.

glosses: To order or assist (to a location), using telecommunications.

examples.text: “Could you call them here? I'd like to talk to them. Or if they're out in the field, radio them in.”
When I told him that they weren't back yet, he asked if we could radio them back early […] Radioing them in was fine with me.
When she arrived, she was told that Tad wasn't there and to have a seat and wait while they radioed him in.
